text:
alex_t: heads-up: code freeze in 2h for v1.8.0 cut. please avoid merges unless you have an approved late-merge exception. if you think you need one, post a quick rationale + rollback plan here and ping me. branch = `release/1.8.0`

release-bot: [automated] code freeze scheduled at <2026-03-17T16:00:00Z> for v1.8.0. exceptions allowed only for critical fixes. see #eng-releases for policy.

maria_g: quick q — do we need a version bump PR merged before freeze for the docs site? PR is #5490 (docs: version → 1.8.0).

alex_t: docs-only bump is fine to land before freeze if it's truly no-behavior change. please annotate the PR with `docs-only` and `changelog-ready` labels and add a short note in the changelog section. no migration code allowed.

cheng_w: i'm looking at PR #5523 (runtime: small kv-cache tweak). tests pass locally but e2e is flaky. we hit a race in staging. how strict are we about that?

alex_t: runtime changes are risky. If this is a perf fix with no API change and you can demo a clean rollback (cherry-pick revert on `main`), we can consider an exception. You must: 1) open an exception request comment in this thread, 2) add `late-merge-exception` label, 3) get @cheng_w + @maria_g QA signoff, 4) include a one-command rollback in the PR description.

samir_k: small docs cherry-pick to release branch — is that allowed without exception? it's just README tweak (PR #5527).

alex_t: docs-only small fixes ok without exception but keep it light. if it touches any config or deploy scripts, treat as code and follow exception flow.

tessa: CI queue is backed up; one flaky integration is blocking staging. If someone requests an exception, do we have a way to prioritize their CI runs?

alex_t: we will not short-circuit CI for exceptions. Exception approval is about allowing a merge once required checks are green. If CI is flaky, try rerun + quick local smoke. Ops (cc @tessa) will triage queue priority, but don't assume bypass.

cheng_w: filing an exception for #5523 — summary: "kv-cache race causing rare tail latency spike in 512-seq workloads", risk: moderate, rollback: revert commit abc123, owner: @cheng_w, QA steps: run `./scripts/smoke_kv.sh` and validate tail p95 < 250ms. pinging for review.

alex_t: received. tagging release lead. please also add that to the PR description and include a staging trace link. I'll vet with @maria_g.

maria_g: reviewed the notes, ok to approve exception if staging smoke passes within 30m. Please post smoke results here.

release-bot: [automated] exception request recorded: ticket RID-1781. maintainers: @alex_t.

alex_t: checklist for exception requests (copy/paste into your exception comment):
```
- PR: <link>
- Risk: (low/med/high)
- Rollback command: `git revert <commit>` / one-liner
- Owner: @your-name
- QA steps & acceptance criteria
- Staging trace link
```

cheng_w: smoke passed — p95 180ms on staging, trace: https://staging.traces/r/abc123. updating PR.

alex_t: good — i'll approve and merge once the clock hits freeze if nothing else changes. thanks. :thumbsup:
